newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas firms on weather, stock refills.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas firms on weather, stock refills.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices were steady to higher Wednesday as much cooler weather was forecast to return to the East Friday and storage injections continued in the West, industry sources said.
Louisiana Gulf Coast gas prices rose two cents to the high-$1.90s to low-$2 area, with Transco (Station 65) quoted at $2.05-2.10 and Henry Hub at $2.00-2.02 per mmBtu.
Prices in south Texas climbed to as high as $1.97 in early trade but then settled back into the low-$1.90s shortly before nomination deadlines.
At the New York City-gate, where temperatures were expected to run six to 12 degrees Fahrenheit below normal Friday, Saturday and again on Monday, prices regained about five cents to $2.34-2.39.
In congruence with Gulf values, Appalachian prices were up three cents at $2.22-2.24 on Columbia and high-$2.20s on CNG.

In the Midcontinent, prices held in the mid-$1.80s, with Demarcation quoted in the low-$1.90s early and the high-$1.80s late. Temperatures in the region are expected to remain cooler-than-normal in the upper Midwest through the weekend.
Chicago city-gate prices were also talked about five cents lower at $2.04-2.07.

Further west, Permian basin prices were steady in the mid-to-high $1.80s as storage injections continued at a fairly steady pace. Waha values were quoted at $1.90-1.92, while southern California border prices were little changed at $1.96-1.99.
Estimates for today's American Gas Association storage report were mostly -5 to -15 bcf.
